L107: # Load
L108: 
L109: Your data can be stored in various places; they can be on your local machine’s disk, in a Github repository, and in in-memory data structures like Python dictionaries and Pandas DataFrames. Wherever a dataset is stored, 🤗 Datasets can help you load it.
L110: 
L111: This guide will show you how to load a dataset from:
L112: 
L113:   * The Hugging Face Hub
L114:   * Local files
L115:   * In-memory data
L116:   * Offline
L117:   * A specific slice of a split
L118: For more details specific to loading other dataset modalities, take a look at the 【52†load audio dataset guide】, the 【55†load image dataset guide】, the 【62†load video dataset guide】, or the 【67†load text dataset guide】.

L81: # DuckDB
L82: 
L83: 【53†DuckDB†duckdb.org】 is a database that supports reading and querying Parquet files really fast. Begin by creating a connection to DuckDB, and then install and load the 【54†`httpfs`†duckdb.org】 extension to read and write remote files:
L84: 
L85: Python
L86: 
L87: JavaScript
L88: Copied
L89: 
L90:     import duckdb
L91: 
L92:     url = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/tasksource/blog_authorship_corpus/resolve/refs%2Fconvert%2Fparquet/default/train/0000.parquet"
L93: 
L94:     con = duckdb.connect()
L95:     con.execute("INSTALL httpfs;")
L96:     con.execute("LOAD httpfs;")
L97: 
L98: Now you can write and execute your SQL query on the Parquet file:
L99: 
L100: Python
L101: 
L102: JavaScript
L103: Copied
L104: 
L105:     con.sql(f"SELECT sign, count(*), AVG(LENGTH(text)) AS avg_blog_length FROM '{url}' GROUP BY sign ORDER BY avg_blog_length DESC LIMIT(5)")
L106:     ┌───────────┬──────────────┬────────────────────┐
L107:     │   sign    │ count_star() │  avg_blog_length   │
L108:     │  varchar  │    int64     │       double       │
L109:     ├───────────┼──────────────┼────────────────────┤
L110:     │ Cancer    │        38956 │ 1206.5212034089743 │
L111:     │ Leo       │        35487 │ 1180.0673767858652 │
L112:     │ Aquarius  │        32723 │ 1152.1136815084192 │
L113:     │ Virgo     │        36189 │ 1117.1982094006466 │
L114:     │ Capricorn │        31825 │  1102.397360565593 │

L104: Managed Agents
L105: 
L106: Always on Cache entries use a 5-minute lifetime by default, and cache reads and writes show up in the session’s usage.
L107: 
L108: Prompt caching optimizes your API usage by letting the API resume from specific prefixes in your prompts. This significantly reduces processing time and costs for repetitive tasks or prompts with consistent elements.
L109: 
L110: There are two ways to enable prompt caching:
